report.summary: Chunk 4 of 6: conductance_report and eigengap_report functions with detailed docstrings and implementation.
risks: conductance_report | medium | The docstring claims 'RANK BY THIS ONE' for leak_rate, but the function returns a dict with rows sorted by leak_rate descending; no external ranking is enforced. Settle by checking if callers use the sorted order.

eigengap_report | medium | Docstring describes behavior for disconnected graphs (zero eigenvalues) but implementation not fully visible in this chunk; the claim about component-free reading is uncheckable. Settle by reviewing full function.

eigengap_report | low | Docstring mentions 'confident' key but implementation not shown; claim about 'confident' being False when gap is not meaningful is uncheckable. Settle by reviewing full function.

handoff.purpose: Implements conductance_report and part of eigengap_report with extensive docstrings.

symbols.name: conductance_report
symbols.note: Computes per-package leak rate and symmetric conductance; returns sorted list of rows.

symbols.name: eigengap_report
symbols.note: Partial implementation; computes eigengap heuristic for cluster count.

claims.text: ``leak_rate`` is ``cut(S) / vol(S)`` -- of all the edge-endpoints this package has, the share that point outside it.
claims.why: Line 390: leak = cut / volume, where volume = nx.volume(graph, inside).
Line 395: symmetric = round(cut / floor, 6) if floor else None, where floor = min(volume, outside_volume).

claims.text: It is reported for cross-reference and it is NOT the ranking key
claims.why: Rows are sorted by leak_rate (line 407-408), not by symmetric.

claims.text: Sorted worst-first, because the only reason to read this list is to find the top of it.
claims.why: Line 407-408: rows.sort(key=lambda r: (-(r['leak_rate'] if r['leak_rate'] is not None else -1.0), r['package'])) sorts descending leak_rate.

claims.text: Packages that are the whole graph, or that have zero volume, are reported with ``leak_rate: None`` rather than a fabricated number.
claims.why: Lines 379-384: if not outside or volume == 0, rows.append with leak_rate: None.

claims.text: Guarded rather than delegated: nx.conductance divides by min(vol(S), vol(rest)) and raises ZeroDivisionError when the rest of the graph is all isolated nodes. A crash is not a measurement.
claims.why: Line 394: floor = min(volume, outside_volume); line 395: symmetric = round(cut / floor, 6) if floor else None avoids division by zero.

claims.text: The normalized Laplacian's eigenvalues are sorted ascending; the largest gap between consecutive eigenvalues at position ``k`` says 'there are k clusters' (the eigengap heuristic).
claims.why: Implementation not shown in this chunk; no code to verify eigenvalue computation or gap selection.

claims.text: Zero eigenvalues count connected components exactly, so a disconnected graph's answer is dominated by them -- the component-free reading over the largest component is reported alongside.
claims.why: Implementation not shown; no code handling zero eigenvalues or component-free reading.

claims.text: ``confident`` is the honest brake: it is False when the winning gap is not meaningfully larger than the runner-up, i.e. when the heuristic is guessing.
claims.why: Implementation not shown; no confident key or gap comparison logic in this chunk.

observations.what: conductance_report uses nx.volume and nx.cut_size from networkx; these are imported from nx (likely networkx).
The function returns a dict with keys 'available', 'packages', 'rows'. The 'packages' key is the number of rows, not the number of packages in partition (skipped packages are not counted).
The docstring of conductance_report claims 'RANK BY THIS ONE' for leak_rate, but the function merely returns a sorted list; ranking is left to the caller.
eigengap_report is incomplete in this chunk; only early validation and docstring are shown.
